ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the view labeled FRONT on the left in the figure is composed of 3 unit squares; on the bottom layer there are 2 squares adjacent left and right, and above the left bottom square there is also 1 square, so viewed from the front the heights of the two columns are respectively 2 and 1. The view labeled SIDE on the right is also composed of 3 unit squares; on the bottom layer there are 2 squares adjacent left and right, and above the right bottom square there is also 1 square, so viewed from the side the heights of the two depth positions are respectively 1 and 2. Then reason: let the left-right positions of the front view be x, and the left-right positions of the side view be y. In order to simultaneously satisfy height 2 of the left column of the front view and height 2 of the right column of the side view, a vertical stack of height 2 can be placed at the intersection position, which requires 2 cubes. It is also necessary to satisfy that the right column of the front view has a block at the bottom and the left column of the side view has a block at the bottom; if only 1 more cube is placed, then it must be placed at the opposite diagonal bottom-cell position. Thus when the total number is 3, that single bottom-cell cube and the height-2 stack are adjacent only in the diagonal direction and do not share a face, therefore violating the condition that “each cube shares at least one face with another cube.” Adding the 4th bottom-layer cube as a bridging block can make all cubes have face contact, while not changing the front view or side view. Therefore at least 4 cubes are needed.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the front view has two bottom squares and one upper square above the left bottom square, so its two front columns have heights 2 and 1. The side view has two bottom squares and one upper square above the right bottom square, so its two depth columns have heights 1 and 2. Let x be the front left/right position and y be the side left/right position. The top-height requirements can be combined by placing a height-2 stack at the intersection of the front-left column and the side-right column; this uses 2 cubes and accounts for both upper squares. The remaining front-right bottom square and side-left bottom square can be covered by one cube at the opposite diagonal base cell, giving a 3-cube projection minimum. However, that cube is diagonally separated from the height-2 stack and shares no face with it. Since the text requires every cube to share a face with another cube, add one bottom cube in one of the other base cells as a face-sharing bridge. This does not change either view, so 4 cubes are sufficient and the previous argument shows 3 is impossible.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a mirrored pair of L-shaped views: front has an upper square only over the left bottom square, while side has an upper square only over the right bottom square. Try to prove whether 3 cubes could work. The upper front square and upper side square must be the same top cube, located at the intersection of the front-left position and the side-right position, and it must have a supporting cube directly below it. That already uses 2 cubes in one vertical stack. A third cube would have to create both missing bottom projections: the front-right bottom square and the side-left bottom square. Therefore it would have to sit at the base position that is front-right and side-left. But that position is diagonal from the base of the vertical stack, so the third cube shares no face with the stack. If instead the third cube were placed face-adjacent to the stack, it could create either the missing front-right projection or the missing side-left projection, but not both. Hence 3 cubes cannot satisfy both the views and the face-sharing condition. With 4 cubes, place the vertical stack at front-left/side-right and use two adjacent bottom cubes to cover front-right and side-left while forming a connected base path. Thus the minimum is 4.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中左边标为 FRONT 的正视图由 3 个单位方格组成：底层有左、右两个方格，上层只有左边一个方格。右边标为 SIDE 的侧视图也是 3 个单位方格，但方向相反：底层有左、右两个方格，上层只有右边一个方格。

推理：把正视图的水平位置记为 front-left 和 front-right，把侧视图的水平位置记为 side-left 和 side-right。上层在正视图中只能出现在 front-left，同时在侧视图中只能出现在 side-right，所以唯一的上层立方体必须位于 front-left 与 side-right 的交叉位置。这个上层立方体不能悬空或只与不存在的上层邻居相连，因此它下面必须有一个立方体作为同一竖直柱的一部分。这样已经用了 2 个立方体。

若只用 3 个立方体，第三个立方体还必须同时补出正视图底层的 front-right 方格和侧视图底层的 side-left 方格，所以它必须放在 front-right 与 side-left 的交叉底层位置。但这个位置与竖直柱底部的 front-left/side-right 位置只是对角相邻，不共享一个面，因此第三个立方体不会和已有立方体共享面，违反题目条件。若第三个立方体改放在与竖直柱底部面相邻的位置，则它只能补出 front-right 或 side-left 其中一个，不能同时满足两个视图。因此 3 个不可能。

4 个可以做到：在 front-left/side-right 位置放一根 2 个立方体的竖直柱，再在底层放两个相邻立方体，例如放在 front-right/side-right 和 front-right/side-left。这样底层正视图有 left 与 right，侧视图有 left 与 right；上层只出现在正视图 left 和侧视图 right；并且所有立方体都至少与另一个立方体共享一个面。所以最少需要 4 个立方体。
